claims.text: In the case \(i=j=p=2,c=6\), one has \(a=\min(p,c)=2\), \(b=2\), and \(N=\binom42=6\). Using the accepted generation input, the two six-element families are \(\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\}\) and \(\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}\). Their images induce surjections \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\). By the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion, each is a basis of \(Q\); hence no proper subfamily generates \(Q\), and therefore no proper subfamily generates \(J_{2,6}\). Thus both families are minimal for this case.
